clue.text: Trooper capturing us in headlong retreat

indicators.note: the headlong retreat holds the word us within it, as captors hold a prisoner
a retreat goes backwards, so the synonym for headlong is read in reverse

parts.note: headlong means rash, acting without thought
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cavalryman rides off in a hasty withdrawal with the rest of us in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headlong' looks like an adverb of the retreat, but it is the adjective giving the synonym that 'retreat' turns round, making HSAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar is a light cavalry soldier, and a trooper is a private in a cavalry regiment.

clue.text: One's naturally irritating in breaking into man's flat

parts.note: his means belonging to a man

indicators.note: the short word bursts into the middle of the word for flat

parts.note: tame means dull or flat, lacking spirit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A burglar breaking into a man's apartment is naturally irksome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' is not an apartment but dull, TAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Histamine is a compound the body releases that causes itching and inflammation.

clue.text: Detective writer shows people gaining nothing in crime

indicators.note: the people and nothing sit inside the word for crime

parts.note: a sin is a wrong or offence
men means people
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A crime novelist depicts folk getting nowhere in wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: Georges Simenon was the Belgian author of the Maigret novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Simenon wrote the Inspector Maigret crime novels.

clue.text: Pronounces prayers to protect monarch

indicators.note: the prayers surround the monarch, shielding it

parts.note: Aves are Ave Marias, Hail Mary prayers
R is for Rex or Regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: People recite prayers for the safety of the sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to declare or state firmly.

clue.text: Old-fashioned style of jumper that's available for a snip

explanation.surface: An outdated knitwear design is on sale cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumper is a high jumper, not a sweater: the scissors was a high-jump technique before the modern back-first flop.
explanation.definitionFit: The scissors is a dated high-jump style with legs crossing in mid-air; scissors are also the tool you snip with.

clue.text: Agreement one may have in the bag

definitions.text: one may have in the bag

explanation.surface: A deal might be something you carry in your bag.
explanation.walkthrough: The bag is a postbag: letters received are this.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence means a match or agreement between things, and also letters, as found in a postbag.

clue.text: Works hard, taking the way north in going up to university

indicators.note: in a down clue going up reads the letters from bottom to top, backwards
the hard workers take the way north inside them

parts.note: sweats means toils or works hard
RD is short for road, a way

explanation.surface: A student slogs, heading north to start at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' puts RDN into SWEATS, making SWERDNATS; 'going up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: St Andrews is Scotland's oldest university, in Fife.

clue.text: Tolbooth, for example, with hellish overseer

explanation.surface: An old Scottish town jail is paired with a demonic supervisor.
explanation.walkthrough: A tolbooth was a Scottish town hall that served as a jail; nick is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A disused jail is a prison of old days; the devil is the overlord of hell.

clue.text: Power cut in secure part of plant

indicators.note: power is cut into the word for secure, entering its middle

parts.note: to seal is to secure or close
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A power failure hits a safe area of a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory but is botanical.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepal is one of the leaf-like parts enclosing a flower bud.

clue.text: Gradually get through between minis

indicators.note: the word for through sits between the two small words

parts.note: mini means small or little, and the plural gives two of them
the second mini, again little
by means through, as in by means of

explanation.surface: Slowly, someone squeezes between small cars.
explanation.walkthrough: Minis are small British cars; plural, they give two LITTLEs.
explanation.definitionFit: Little by little means in small steps, slowly over time.

clue.text: Work out the bill? Be reasonable!

explanation.surface: A diner asks for the total, then pleads with the waiter about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To total a bill is to sum its items; an argument that makes sense is one that holds together logically.

clue.text: A long time to accept new girl

indicators.note: the long time takes in another letter, accepting it into the middle

parts.note: ages is a colloquial word for a long time

explanation.surface: It takes forever to welcome a newcomer, a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is a female first name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Grinding routine offering no hope of progress

definitions.text: Grinding routine offering no hope of progress

parts.words: Grinding routine offering no hope of progress
parts.note: literally a mill wheel walked by people or animals to grind corn, going nowhere; figuratively a dreary job

explanation.definitionFit: A tedious job with no advancement is likened to a wheel trodden endlessly in one place.

clue.text: Lawyers' holy of holies?

parts.note: the innermost sanctuary of a temple, read as the name of one of the London Inns of Court where barristers belong

explanation.walkthrough: The Inns of Court are the four London societies every English barrister must join; one bears this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The innermost shrine of a temple is its holiest room, and the London barristers' society takes that name.

clue.text: Thinking one's supposed to be on one's bike

definitions.text: supposed to be on one's bike

explanation.surface: A person reckons they are meant to be cycling.
explanation.walkthrough: A reflector is a thinker; it is also the red reflective plate a bicycle must carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A meditative person ponders; a bicycle carries a rear reflecting plate by law.

clue.text: 50% of Japanese clothing is novel in India

indicators.note: half of the letters of the Japanese garment, taking the first three of six

explanation.surface: Half of a Japanese wardrobe turns up as a book set on the subcontinent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's novel about an orphan boy in British India bears this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudyard Kipling's 1901 novel follows an Irish orphan on the roads of British India.

clue.text: Malt -a unit to be drunk at start of day

indicators.note: being drunk muddles these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A measure of malt whisky to be downed first thing in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Matutinal means relating to or happening in the early morning.

clue.text: Measure of work that's so short

indicators.note: the Latin word for therefore is cut short by losing its last letter

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, meaning so

explanation.surface: A job's output is so brief.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics an erg is a small unit of work or energy in the centimetre-gram-second system.

clue.text: Finally silencing noise in tummy, getting beef

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word silencing is taken

parts.note: a rumble is the sound of a hungry stomach

explanation.surface: At last quieting a stomach's growl by eating beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' is slang for a complaint, not meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef in slang means a complaint, as does a moan or gripe.

clue.text: Initial advantage the Wrights gave us

explanation.surface: Early aviation pioneers gave humanity a head start.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wright brothers made the first powered aeroplane flights in 1903, starting off the age of flying.
explanation.definitionFit: A head start in a race is a quick getaway; the Wrights literally began human powered flight.

clue.text: I have to hold up a vehicle that's causing injury

indicators.note: in a down clue the item that holds another up sits under it

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A robber stops a coach in a way that's harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold up' looks like a robbery; it means IVE supports A BUS from below.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusive treatment is harmful, insulting or cruel.

clue.text: Iron I use — how badly at first, possibly

definitions.text: Iron I use — how badly at first, possibly

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come at first, before the metal's symbol
these words are done badly, so their letters come out in a jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A homemaker admits that early on, they used the iron clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue pictures a novice homemaker struggling with the ironing; 'possibly' marks the definition as one example, and 'at first' places the jumbled HOUSEWI before the metal's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A homemaker who irons the household linen is pictured, someone running a home perhaps clumsily when new.

clue.text: Hotel used by majority of most common element

indicators.note: most but not all of the element's name is kept, losing its end

parts.note: hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe

explanation.surface: An inn is fed by most of the commonest gas.
explanation.walkthrough: A hydro is a hotel offering spa treatments, from 'hydropathic'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydro is a spa hotel offering water cures.

clue.text: Clamour when one puts on dry coat

I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone makes a racket while pulling on a weatherproof jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts on' and 'coat' together put I inside BRUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruit is an old word for noise, rumour or report, so it suits loud clamour.

clue.text: From Harris's brother, I accepted pipe

indicators.note: the brother takes in the letter I

parts.note: Brer is the 'brother' title in Joel Chandler Harris's Uncle Remus stories, as in Brer Rabbit

explanation.surface: A man takes a pipe from a sibling of someone called Harris.
explanation.definitionFit: A brier is a tobacco pipe carved from briar root.

clue.text: One who used to go to court to appeal for what's owed

parts.words: One who used to go to court

it is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A former courtier lodges an appeal over money due.
explanation.walkthrough: Debutantes were presented to the monarch at court until 1958, hence 'used to'. The court is royal, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: A debit is an entry recording a sum owing on an account.

clue.text: Repeatedly I act flexibly to meet new end?

definitions.text: Repeatedly I act flexibly to meet new end?

indicators.note: acting flexibly suggests bending these letters into a new shape
the words I act are taken more than once, here twice over

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A planner keeps adapting to reach a fresh goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' doubles I ACT; with N those letters are bent by 'flexibly' into the answer. The whole clue describes someone who adapts their methods to win an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategist or planner adapts manoeuvres flexibly to achieve each objective as it arises.

clue.text: Unidentified person with gun is a sort of bandit

parts.note: one means an unspecified person, as in one never knows
someone carrying a gun is armed

explanation.surface: An anonymous gunman is some kind of outlaw.
explanation.walkthrough: A one-armed bandit is a slot machine with a pull lever, so the answer describes this type of bandit.
explanation.definitionFit: Slot machines are nicknamed one-armed bandits for their single lever and the cash they take.

clue.text: Trying situation soldiers have to negotiate

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Troops face a testing spell of negotiations.
